title: Offset for the Primary Policy’s Own Loss-of-Use Cover on Excess Flood Claims
content:
The **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** layer pays loss of use above the primary policy's own loss-of-use cover.

**Rule.** The underlying offset keeps the excess layer above the primary policy's own loss-of-use cover: where the underlying policy number on the policy record is that of a Tidemark HomeFlood policy, the offset is the loss-of-use limit of that HomeFlood policy's tier; where the underlying is a private primary policy of another carrier, the offset is 10 percent of the underlying dwelling limit on the policy record; and otherwise, for an underlying NFIP Dwelling Form policy, which carries no loss-of-use cover, there is no underlying offset and loss of use is paid from the first dollar.

The HomeFlood policy read is the one in HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record; the offset is the loss-of-use limit that product's tier carries for that policy. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

Every share or period cut multiplies the loss of use counted; every amount deducted is then subtracted, never taking the figure below nothing; every allowance is then added; the loss-of-use limit then caps the result; payments already issued on the claim are subtracted after the cap; and every interest charge is added last.

| Underlying named on the excess policy record | Underlying offset |
|---|---|
| a Tidemark HomeFlood policy | the loss-of-use limit of that HomeFlood policy's tier |
| a private primary policy of another carrier | 10 percent (0.1) of the underlying dwelling limit on the excess policy record |
| an NFIP Dwelling Form policy | none; loss of use paid from the first dollar |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** Over a private primary policy of another carrier with an underlying dwelling limit of 300000, the offset is 30000; a loss of use counted of 22000 after any share or cut leaves nothing after the offset, never a negative figure.
